sentence: Fexofenadine is an antihistamine medicine that relieves the symptoms of allergies.
The NHS lists hay fever, conjunctivitis, eczema, hives, insect bite and sting reactions and some food allergies among the problems it is used for.
MedlinePlus describes it as treating allergy symptoms such as a runny nose, sneezing, and red, itchy or watery eyes, as well as itching and redness caused by hives.

A leaflet for the branded product Telfast says it is used in adults and adolescents aged 12 and over to relieve itching, swelling and rashes from long-term allergic skin reactions known as chronic idiopathic urticaria.
MedlinePlus has a separate page for products that combine fexofenadine with pseudoephedrine, which are different products from fexofenadine on its own.
note: Separate MedlinePlus page title 'Fexofenadine and Pseudoephedrine'; 'different product' is the search summary's note.

sentence: Fexofenadine blocks histamine, a substance in the body that drives allergy symptoms.
The NHS says that by blocking the effects of histamine it reduces the symptoms, and that people should start to feel better within 1 to 2 hours.
A 2024 review describes it as a non-sedating, second-generation H1 antihistamine.
note: Attribution to which PMC review not separable.

sentence: The NHS classes fexofenadine as non-drowsy and says it seems less likely to cause sleepiness than other non-drowsy antihistamines.
It also says fexofenadine is unlikely to cause harm when used for a long time, though it is best taken only for as long as it is needed.
